live.modulate~ adds an offset to the "nominal" value of a parameter, i.e the current value. Using the Live API, we can get the minimum and maximum value for that parameter and patch together a mode in which the modulation source modulates the parameter between the minimum and the current value. This "multiplicative" modulation can be useful for parameters where you don't want to exceed the current value, such as for Volume / Gains Faders.

live.modulate~ receives a signal between -1 and 1 in the left inlet.

The amount of modulation applied depends on the modulation type of the parameter.

For bipolar modulation, the input range (-1 to 1) is equal to the range of the parameter (minimum - maximum). This means if you're current value on the parameter, for example a dial, is set to the minimum, a modulation value of 1.0 will result in modulated value at the parameter's maximum.

The live.modulate~ object has an input range of -1 to 1 which maps onto the full range of the modulated parameter. You can control the depth of the modulation with the depth attribute. In other words, you can constrain the modulation to a smaller amount than the full range, expressed as a depth amount between 0 and 1.

The live.modulate~ object reports if the mapping was successful or not from the first outlet. If the mapping was successful it outputs "mapped 1", if it is unsuccessful it outputs "mapped 0".

You can use this to handle instances where someone tries to map to a parameter that is already mapped, for example.

Setting a smoothing value will result in value changes being sent to Live as a ramp, so the value will be reached in the time specifed by the smoothing value. This allows smooth control of Live's parameters without overflowing the communication by sending events for each sample.
